subject: SCIM handover playbook + SAML samples — timeline & deliverables
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acmeid.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmeid.com
Date: Sun, 5 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: SCIM delta + SAML assertion samples for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Vanessa,

We're running through our SIG/CAIQ pack and need a compact handover of your SCIM provisioning details and a few SAML assertion examples for our auditors. Specifically: 
- A delta export (CSV) showing changes over the last 30 days (adds/updates/deletes)
- Example SAML assertions for a service account and a regular user (headers + sample attributes)
- A short description of RBAC roles mapping (who maps to admin/operator/viewer)

Can you share a deliverable plan and an ETA? Our internal deadline for the review is EOD Sep 10. If you need us to accept an interim bundle, say so.

Thanks,
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Security Operations
Acme ID

Attachment: requested-fields-sig.xlsx (referenced)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acmeid.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 5 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCIM delta + SAML assertion samples for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. We can meet the Sep 10 review target with a staged delivery. High level plan below: 

1) Today (Sep 5): Share a SCIM delta CSV (last 30 days) + a compressed sample SAML assertion text file for review.
2) Sep 6: Provide RBAC role mapping worksheet and an abbreviated handover playbook (procedures, redaction notes).
3) Sep 7: Finalized package (PDF playbook + spreadsheets) and a short executive summary for auditors.

Who will accept the interim bundle? If Security Team can confirm, we'll drop the initial ZIP to the Drive link and send a DocuSign acknowledgement for your records.

Attachments (will include in first drop): scim-delta-sample-20270905.csv; saml-assertion-examples-20270905.txt

I'll loop in Jonas for the RBAC mapping and Laura for any privileged account proofs.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: scim-delta-sample-20270905.csv (CSV), saml-assertion-examples-20270905.txt (text)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acmeid.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCIM delta + SAML assertion samples for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi all — adding the RBAC detail here. A few notes for the auditors and for Acme's mapping exercise: 

- We maintain role definitions in a central RBAC sheet; roles are organized by privilege boundary (Admin / PlatformOps / AppOwner / ReadOnly).
- Mapping guidance: Admin => full org-level operations (can manage SCIM connectors), PlatformOps => can rotate service keys and run JIT reconciliations, AppOwner => app-level provisioning rights, ReadOnly => audit-only.
- For this handover I've prepared an RBAC mapping workbook (rbac-mapping-roles-20270906.xlsx) that contains: canonical role names, example Azure AD groups, SCIM group attribute key, and a delta reconciliation column.
- We redacted PII from the SCIM delta export; the CSV includes hashed user IDs and event_type (create/update/delete), timestamp, source, and target_group attributes.

Laura — for the privileged account proof we can either include a snapshot of service-account bindings or provide a short attestation. Which does Acme prefer?

- Jonas
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: rbac-mapping-roles-20270906.xlsx

From: Security Team <security@acmeid.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acmeid.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCIM delta + SAML assertion samples for SIG/CAIQ review

Thanks — this looks good. A couple follow-ups before you finalize: 
- Can you confirm total monthly active user count (approx) so we can size sampling? (ballpark is fine)
- For the service-account assertion, please include the audience (aud) and nameID format you use; our auditors want to see assertion semantics.
- We prefer the snapshot for privileged accounts (one CSV with bindings) rather than a text attestation.

If you can get the interim bundle into the Drive link you shared and drop a short checklist in the Jira ticket SEC-789, we can begin consuming the artifacts this afternoon.

—Acme Security Ops

Referenced: Jira SEC-789

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Security Team <security@acmeid.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acmeid.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCIM delta + SAML assertion samples for SIG/CAIQ review

All — final update and delivery plan: 

Delivered now to Drive (link below):
- scim-delta-sample-20270905.csv (hashed IDs, event_type, timestamp, source, target_group)
- saml-assertion-examples-20270905.txt (service-account + user assertions with aud and nameID examples)
- rbac-mapping-roles-20270906.xlsx (canonical roles + Azure AD group mappings)
- privilege-bindings-20270907.csv (service-account bindings snapshot)
- handover-playbook-v1.0.pdf (procedural steps, retention notes, redaction approach)

We also added a short checklist into SEC-789 and created a DocuSign acknowledgment so your audit team can sign-off on receipt if required: https://www.docusign.com/en/sessions/abcd-1234

Monthly active users (approx): 18k — we've included that ballpark in the executive summary.

Next steps: please confirm once the auditors have consumed the artifacts or if they need additional SAML attributes. Happy to jump on a 30-minute sync with your team to walk through samples.

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
